Alex — really glad the demo was useful. High-level answers and we'll follow with a short proposal and SOW draft by Friday. Quick summary: 

- Premium: typical single-tenant premium ranges from 25–40% over our shared Dedicated pricing depending on isolation scope (VPC-only vs fully isolated GPU pool + dedicated control plane + HSM/KMS).
- Sizing: we use a combination of target p99 latency, qps distribution, and token-per-request estimates. - Throughput SLOs: we can offer SLO-backed commitments on latency tiers for reserved commits; credits are possible but limited to outages caused by Redwood-controlled infra.
- KMS & audit logs: customer KMS integration (bring-your-own) and audit log exports are included for Private deployments; HSM-backed key wraps are treated as an optional advanced feature (added cost due to third-party HSM fees).

Rachel — quick technical sizing notes for the proposal: 

- Model assumption: production plan will use a quantized Llama-3-70B-4bit style variant optimized for throughput (approx 14–18 tokens/sec/GPU under continuous batching). If Infinia opts for a higher-accuracy fp16 variant we'll need ~1.6x GPUs.
- Workload profile: 600 qps sustained with average request = 60 tokens; peak 1k qps. Using continuous batching and prefix caching, net token/sec estimate: sustained token/sec = 600 * 60 = 36k tps. At 16 tps/GPU (conservative), requires 2250 GPU-token-seconds -> approx 14 GPUs sustained. Add 30% buffer for peaks/maintenance -> 18 GPUs.
- We propose a 20 GPU private pool as starting SKU (allows headroom + rolling upgrades). Reserved commit options: 12-month or 36-month terms; longer term allows deeper discounts.
- HSM/KMS: we can integrate customer KMS for key wrapping at no recurring charge, but HSM (FIPS-certified appliances) incurs one-time provisioning + monthly service fee (~$1.2k/mo depending on provider).
- Throughput SLO: for 20-GPU pool we can offer a 99th percentile latency SLO for configured model at 95% of baseline throughput. Credits: standard schedule (1 day SLA breach = 5% credit up to cap).

I recommend quoting 3 tiers: 20 GPU reserved (baseline), 30 GPU reserved (for headroom), and 20 GPU with burst buffer to shared capacity (cheaper but reduced isolation).

Ben
